features.summary: Video decoding was refined across FFmpeg, Android, and Vulkan: FFmpeg now handles image creation and seek thresholds more consistently, and Android decoder shutdown avoids a lingering reference. Platform-specific workarounds and compatibility checks were also narrowed or updated, reducing the risk of playback issues on affected systems.

It also checks that Android can create the needed cryptography before starting playback and uses the correct property for Widevine’s service certificate.

features.summary: MP4 seeking now reads the relevant stream fragments before looking up a keyframe, counts skipped samples more accurately, and can retry from an earlier keyframe if playback reaches the end of available data too soon. The updates also read constant encryption values from protected sample groups, helping seeks work correctly in fragmented and encrypted MP4 files.

features.summary: Media Source Extensions (MSE), which let web pages assemble and play media streams, now have test coverage for seeking across different keyframe layouts. The MSE test helper can also run after the page has loaded, making it more flexible for browser tests.

features.summary: Firefox no longer triggers autoplay notifications while its garbage collector is running. This avoids notification work at an inappropriate point during browser memory cleanup.

features.summary: HTMLMediaElement.captureStream(), which lets a page capture media playback as a MediaStream, now requests a SystemClockDriver to keep the stream’s timing moving. This helps captured audio and video stay coordinated even when the media graph has no audio device driving its clock.
